steps: Unpack & fit the barrier screen
Check the crate, free the barrier screen from the pallet and hang it on the door hinge bosses; fit the backup batteries before connecting power.

1. Inspect the shipping crate; tell your dealer at once about any damage.
  2. Safety barrier screen: it ships secured to the pallet. Remove the two screws, break the attachment brackets off at the perforation, then hook the barrier's brackets over the door hinge bosses (doors open or closed).
  3. Lift off the Top Plate. To open the firebox, pull the two Glass Frame Latches on top of the firebox forward out of their notches.
  4. Install the backup batteries before connecting power: the battery box is behind the right side of the control compartment on hook-and-loop tape; press to open the tray.

Hardware bag

Fuel Conversion Kit - LP157467
Rock Wool, 1 oz.157259
Slotted Air Guides157491
Ember Stones224968
1.5v AAA Batteries4

Suggested tools (p. 2): external regulator (propane only), code-compliant piping, manual shut-off valve (T-handle in Massachusetts), sediment trap if required by code, tee joint, pipe wrench, pipe sealant, 10 mm, 1/2" and 7/16" open end wrenches, Phillips and flat head screwdrivers, 1/4" nut driver, Torx T-20, tin snips, gloves, safety glasses.
Site & floor protection
Never directly on carpet, vinyl, linoleum or laminate; on combustibles other than wood, a floor pad the full width and depth of the stove.

Weigh heat distribution, vent termination, gas line routing, and traffic, furniture and draperies; leave access for service.

  • Not directly on carpeting, vinyl, linoleum or wood laminate flooring such as Pergo®.
  • On any combustible other than wood: a floor pad of metal, wood, ceramic tile, stone or a listed hearth pad, the full width and depth of the appliance. Carpet, vinyl or linoleum can stay underneath.
  • Minimum hearth protection is drawn in fig. 1 on this page; read its dimensions there.
  • "Fire resistant" materials and fire-rated sheet rock count as combustible.

Clearances and alcove limits: see the Clearances card (p. 7).
Vent system & exhaust restrictor
One manufacturer's approved components, terminating inside a shaded zone of the matrix; set the exhaust restrictor to that zone (factory: D, fully open).

Approved: M&G DuraVent (Direct Vent Pro Series), American Metal Products (Amerivent), Security Chimneys (Secure Vent), Selkirk Metalbestos (Direct Temp), Metal-Fab (Sure-Seal Direct Vent), Industrial Chimney Corp. (ExcelDirect), Bernard Delsin (Pro Form), Olympia Chimney Supply (Ventis Direct Vent). Don't mix manufacturers.

  • Seal each joint with a 1/8" bead of high-temperature sealant or Mil-Pac on the male section of the inner pipe; no silicone.
  • Its own vent system, direct to the outside; never a chimney serving another appliance.

Exhaust restrictor

  1. Read the termination zone (A–D) from the matrix, fig. 9 on p. 9.
  2. Lift off the Top Plate. At the right side of the firebox top, loosen the pivot-pin nut with a 7 mm or 9/32 nut driver, push the pin left, and move it forward into the slot for your zone.
  3. Tighten the lock nut and refit the Top Plate.

Zone E (terminations between 24-35 feet): setting A plus the Restrictor Extension Plate (Miscellaneous bag) re-installed upside down. On a division line use the less restrictive position (24 ft./5 ft. = Position C). Long runs (over 12 ft.) in uninsulated air space may need CPI mode.

The matrix zones are shown only as a diagram on p. 9; read them from the page.
Mobile home (if applicable)
Secure with Floor Bracket Kit #750304, ground the stove to the chassis, and follow Title 24 CFR Part 3280 or CSA Z240.4.

1. Secure the stove to the floor with Jøtul Floor Bracket Kit #750304.
  2. Provide an electrical ground between the stove and the mobile home chassis.
  3. Install per Title 24 CFR, Part 3280 (U.S.) or CSA Z240.4 (Canada), and check local restrictions.

Approved for aftermarket, permanently located manufactured (mobile) homes where local codes allow, and as an OEM installation.
Fuel conversion (propane)
Ships for natural gas; convert before installing with the included kit 157467: burner orifice, pilot injector, regulator, stop screw and labels.

1. Turn off the gas. Remove the Top Plate, unlatch and lift out the glass frame, then remove the embers, logs (fragile) and Burner Skirt.
  2. Under the stove, loosen the Air Shutter wingnut and push the stem back; remove the four screws and lift out the Burner Plate.
  3. Change the burner orifice with a 1/2" open end wrench or deep-well socket. LP only: install the stop screw in the air shutter plate.
  4. Pilot: remove the pilot head with the 7/16" wrench, holding the bracket so it doesn't bend; swap the injector; refit with the hood aimed at the flame sensor and carry-over ports.
  5. Refit the burner level on its four brackets, engaged with the air shutter.
  6. Regulator: remove the two front screws with a Torx T-20 and fit the kit's regulator.
  7. Apply Label A (back of stove), Label B (rating plate) and the small label (valve).
  8. Reassemble, leak-test, check pressures with a manometer, then set the air shutter, starting from the half-way position.
Gas connection & leak test
3/8" npt to the left side of the valve, with a shut-off valve and union in the same room; brush on soapy water, never a flame.

• Fitting the optional blower? Install it before the gas line to avoid clearance interference.
  • 3/8" npt with a 1/2" diameter supply, or sized to hold pressure at any input setting.
  • Gas shut-off valve (gas cock) and union in the same room; a T-handle gas cock is required in Massachusetts (248CMR).
  • Flexible connectors are acceptable in many U.S. areas; Canadian methods vary. Follow local code, or ANSI Z223.1/NFPA 54 or CAN-B149.
  • Propane: use propane-resistant sealing compounds.

Leak test

  1. Mix a 50-50 solution of water and dish soap.
  2. Light the appliance.
  3. Brush every joint and connection. Bubbles or gas odor: turn the gas off at once, tighten or reconnect, and retest.
Apply with a small brush; a spray bottle can damage the electronics. Never use an open flame to check for leaks.
Massachusetts: installation by a licensed master or journeyman plumber or gas-fitter (p. 2).
Gas pressure & high altitude
Manometer on E (inlet) and A (manifold) with the valve knob on HIGH; never derate natural gas; propane over 2000 ft. may need kit 157471.

• Test points are on the front of the valve: E = inlet (supply), A = manifold. Always test with the valve control knob on HIGH.
  • Supply piping tests above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance; at or below 1/2 psig: close its manual shut-off valve.
  • Propane derate: follow steps 1-8 of the fuel conversion with the kit's injector, then leak and pressure tests, system check and flame picture.
  • Fill out the high altitude conversion label and apply it to the rating plate.

Pressure ranges are on the inlet and manifold cards.
Log set & ember stones
Fit any brick panels first, place the six logs on their pins in order, and keep ember stones clear of the pilot and carry-over ports.

The optional brick panel kit 157458 goes in first, after the proper burner skirt extensions or air guides. The log set must be installed before running the burner. Wear gloves; the logs are fragile.

#1 Rear · 226892over the two pins on the back shelf of the burner skirt
#2 Left Front · 224893, #3 Right Front · 224894on the pins in the center of the burner plate
#4 Right Cross · 224897across the Rear and Right Front logs
#5 Middle Cross · 224896over the Right Cross log and the tip of the Left Front log
#6 Left Cross · 224895over the Rear and Left Front logs

Spread ember stones loosely over the burner plate and around the logs, away from the burner edges. Keep them off the pilot assembly, the burner skirt air openings and the pilot carry-over ports. You don't need them all; too many can promote sooting. Use the rock wool sparingly.

The set packed in the firebox is identified on p. 20 as the #158261 Fiber Log Set (the six pieces above). For a replacement set, the replacement parts list on p. 36 gives Replacement Log Set 157445.
System check & air shutter
Purge the line, confirm a steady pilot that engulfs the top 1/8" of the sensor, check LOW to HIGH, then set the air shutter for a soot-free flame.

1. Purge: the first lighting takes a few moments to clear air from the line. From a cold start, running the pilot in CPI for 10 - 15 minutes helps establish positive draft.
  2. Pilot flame (under the Rear Log): steady, not lifting or floating; blue around the hood with traces of yellow toward the edges; engulfing the top 1/8" of the flame sensor and projecting toward the burner plate carry-over ports. Adjust at the screw left of the valve regulator.
  3. Burner: rotate the regulator knob; flame height changes approximately 50% between LOW and HIGH. No smoke or soot should be present: check log placement, then the air shutter.

Air shutter

Loosen the wingnut under the stove; slide the stud forward for more air, back for less, in small increments. Burn 30 minutes on HIGH watching the flame; repeat if it's weak, slow or sooty, then tighten the wingnut. Too much air gives a blue, transparent ("anemic") flame; too little gives very long yellow flames and soot. On propane the range is limited by the conversion kit's stop screw. More vent offsets mean more need for adjustment.

Air shutter adjustments only by a qualified, professional service technician.
Pair the remote (if fitted)
Press the IFC board's button (three beeps), then ON on the transmitter within 10 seconds; finish with Burner ON and Pilot Mode CPI.

1. Press the Controls Access Door to release its magnetic catch and swing it down. Switch the Burner to OFF.
  2. Put three AAA batteries in the transmitter.
  3. Press the black (or red) button on the right front corner of the IFC board, just behind the switch plate. It beeps three times and a yellow LED marks a 10-second window.
  4. Within 10 seconds, press ON on the transmitter. Four beeps confirm it has taken that transmitter's code.
  5. Set the Burner switch to ON and the Pilot Mode switch to CPI.

To return to full manual operation, hold the button until it beeps three or four times and the yellow LED lights, then within 10 seconds press it again until it acknowledges.

items: Air opening too large: a blue, transparent flame

Ember stones on the pilot assembly or carry-over ports interfere with proper burner function

light.title: Lighting the stove
light.html:
Your stove has an ignition device that lights the pilot automatically. Never try to light the pilot by hand. The switches are behind the controls access door: press the door to release its magnetic catch and swing it down.

  1. Read the safety information. Smell all around the stove for gas, including next to the floor, because some gas is heavier than air.
  2. If you have a thermostat, set it to its lowest setting.
  3. Set the Burner switch to OFF.
  4. Wait five (5) minutes to clear out any gas, then smell again, near the floor too. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps under Safety.
  5. Set the Pilot Mode switch: CPI keeps the pilot lit for up to seven days; IPI lights it only when there is a call for heat.
  6. Set the Burner switch to ON or T-STAT.
  7. Set the thermostat to the setting you want to light the burner.

If it won't run, turn off the gas to the stove and call your service technician or gas supplier.

To turn off the gas to the stove

  1. Set the thermostat to its lowest setting.
  2. If service is to be done, turn off all electric power to the stove.
  3. Set the Burner switch to OFF and close the control access door.
The stove plugs into 120VAC house current with its supplied cord. With the Proflame 2 remote, set Pilot Mode to CPI and Burner to ON, then press the remote's ON/OFF key.

remote.title: Using the Proflame 2 remote
remote.html:
The Proflame 2 Multifunction Remote is an accessory (it also comes with the blower kit). For remote use, set the stove's Pilot Mode switch to CPI and its Burner switch to ON. A single beep from the stove confirms each command.

The keys

  • ON/OFF: the pilot lights, followed shortly by the burner. Press again to shut the burner down.
  • Up / Down: six flame levels. Down steps the flame lower until the burner turns off; Up brings it back on at High.
  • Thermostat: switches between manual and thermostat control. Keep pressing until SMART shows and the stove turns the flame down as the room nears your set temperature.
  • Mode: picks what you're adjusting: pilot mode (CPI/IPI), burner, fan or accent lamp.

Pilot mode: with the remote off, press Mode (IPI is the default), then Up for CPI or Down for IPI.

Child lock: press Mode and Up together; do it again to unlock. Room temperature: with the remote off, press Thermostat and Mode together.

Fan (optional blower): six speeds; set it to ON first. After 5 minutes it runs at top speed, then settles to your setting, and it keeps going for 12 minutes after the burner turns off. Manual fan speed isn't available while SMART is on.

On thermostat, the stove can turn on suddenly and may be very hot even when the burner looks off. Keep the remote where children can't reach it.

firstfire.title: Your first fires
firstfire.html:
The paint and the log set heat-cure the first time the stove runs. That gives off an odor and some visible smoke. It's normal and it passes.

Before the first fire

  • Ventilate: open doors and windows and use a fan to move fresh air through the room.
  • Vacate: the fumes are non-toxic, but they can be uncomfortable for babies, small children, pregnant women, the elderly, pets and anyone with breathing difficulties.

The curing run

Once your installer has confirmed the burner works at all heat levels, run the stove on a high setting for 2-4 hours.

Fog and a white film on the glass

A little condensation can form on the glass each time you light the stove. It clears as the glass heats. After the first few fires you'll also see a white, powdery film on the inside of the glass. Clean it off with a non-abrasive household glass cleaner or warm water, or it can permanently etch the glass.

Don't use ammonia-based cleaners on the glass.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass only when it needs it, and only when it's cool.

  1. Wipe the surface with a clean, dampened, soft cloth.
  2. Follow with a dry, soft towel. Take care not to scratch it.
Never clean the glass while it's hot, and don't use abrasive or ammonia-based cleaners.

The white film after the first fires

A white, powdery residue forms as the burner media cures. Clean it off with a non-abrasive household glass cleaner and warm water. Left on, it can permanently etch the glass.

Reaching the inside

The glass frame lifts out: lift the Top Plate off, pull the two Glass Frame Latches forward, then lift the frame up and out. Lay it on a blanket or towel so it doesn't get scratched. Handle the glass carefully; it can shatter if struck.

Scratches and damage

Scratches weaken the glass. If you find any, have a qualified technician replace the panel with Jøtul part no. 155599. Never run the stove with the glass removed, cracked or broken.

modes.title: Switches & pilot modes
modes.html:
Two switches in the control compartment set how the stove behaves.

Burner switch

ONmanual control of the burner; leave it here for the Proflame 2 remote
T-STATfor an optional wall thermostat or remote transmitter control
OFFturns off both remote and manual burner operation

Switch the burner OFF when you won't use the stove for an extended period.

Pilot mode

IPI (intermittent pilot): the pilot lights only when there is a call for heat.

CPI (continuous pilot): the pilot burns for up to seven days. If there's no call for heat in that time it goes out on its own, then re-ignites at the next call for heat. While it's lit, take care using household products with combustible vapors.

With the remote: leave the stove's switch on CPI; the remote then chooses IPI or CPI, with IPI as its default. Setting the switch to IPI disables that.

From a cold start, letting the pilot burn in CPI for 10 - 15 minutes helps establish draft before the burner comes on. Some long vent runs need CPI; your installer will know.

Flame height by hand: turn the regulator knob in the control compartment. The flame changes about 50% between LOW and HIGH.

sounds.title: Sounds, smells & a clean flame
sounds.html:
Creaking and pinging

Cast iron and steel expand and contract as the temperature changes. The creaks and pings you hear are that natural thermal movement, not a fault.

A slight hum

The optional blower makes a slight hum on its low setting. It gets louder as the fan speeds up.

Smoke and odor early on

Some smoke and odor are normal in the first stages of use while the stove cures. Keep fresh air moving near the stove and it passes.

What the flame should look like

Once it's cured, there should be no smoke or soot. Soot shows up as black deposits on the logs or the inside walls of the stove. If you see it, have a qualified service technician check the log placement and the air shutter. Don't adjust the air shutter yourself.

A gas smell is different. Don't light anything, don't touch electrical switches or use a phone in the building, and call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone.

power.title: Power & batteries
power.html:
The stove's control board runs on 120V house current. If the power goes out, a backup battery pack keeps the burner working, including from the remote. The blower and accent lamp won't run without house power.

Backup packfour 1.5v batteries (size: see below)
Remote transmitter3, AAA - 1.5V
Note: the manual gives the backup battery size as 4, AA - 1.5V on p. 4 (also four, 1.5v AA on p. 28, the p. 32 wiring diagram and the "(4 AA)" battery box on p. 34), and as four 1.5v AAA on the fig. 44 label on p. 24 and in the battery replacement steps on p. 32.

Replacing the backup batteries

A red light on the control board means they're low.

  1. Turn off the main gas supply, switch the Burner to OFF and unplug the stove.
  2. The battery box is behind the right side of the control compartment, held by hook-and-loop tape.
  3. Fit fresh batteries, put the box back and plug the stove in.

The remote

A battery icon appears on its screen before the power runs out. Fit three fresh AAA batteries, and don't press any keys while you do: that turns that function off.

If more than 6 months have passed since the build date on the shipping crate label, be ready to replace the backup batteries.

safety.title: Safety around the stove
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance, and put out any open flame. Open windows.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch or use any phone in your building.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Everyday safety

  • The stove's surfaces get very hot. Keep children and adults away to avoid burns or clothing catching fire, and supervise young children in the room.
  • The barrier screen over the glass must stay on. Put it back after any service, and replace a damaged one with Jøtul's barrier for this stove.
  • For toddlers or other at-risk people, a child guard or an adjustable safety gate is recommended.
  • Keep clothing, furniture, draperies, gasoline and other flammable liquids away from the stove.
  • Burn only natural gas or propane, never wood, paper, cardboard or coal.
  • Don't use the stove if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the stove and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
Massachusetts: a carbon monoxide detector must be installed in the same room as the stove.

service.title: Annual service & cleaning
service.html:
Have a qualified service technician inspect the stove and its venting before use and at least once a year. Gas and power must be off before any service work.

What the yearly service covers

  • The whole vent system, including the chimney, inspected and cleaned.
  • The pilot assembly inspected and cleaned; any corroded part replaced.
  • The glass gasket checked for wear and a good seal, and replaced if needed.

Keeping it clean

  • The firebox and valve compartment should be vacuumed once a year with a soft brush attachment. The logs are fragile, so go gently. Vacuum more often if you have pets.
  • Keep the control compartments and the area under the stove free of dust, and the space around it clear of anything that burns.
  • Make sure the convection airways and the optional blower aren't blocked.
Lint from carpeting or bedding can mean the stove needs cleaning more often.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Jøtul North America's limited warranty covers the original retail purchaser from the date of purchase. It isn't transferable.

Cast iron, steel doors, surround components, firebox5 years
Burner, burner treatments, firebox panels2 years
Enamel finish (peeling or fading)2 years
Gas and electrical parts (controls, plumbing, valve, blower)1 year

Not covered

  • Normal-wear parts: paint, lamp bulbs, gaskets and glass, unless damaged by thermal stress
  • Incorrect installation, or unauthorized modification, use or repair
  • Enamel damage from misuse (bubbling, cracking or discoloration)
  • Labor beyond the warranty period, travel time, loss of service, and damage in transit
The warranty is void if installation or service is done by anyone other than an authorized installer, service agency or gas supplier. Jøtul must receive notice of a possible defect within 60 days of finding it, so contact your nearest authorized Jøtul dealer quickly, and keep your dated sales receipt.

This page also carries a sentence printed only in French beside the high-altitude text; read it on the page.

specVentV.title: Vertical & co-linear venting
specVentV.html:
Total run35 ft. (10.66 m) max
Vertical run8 ft. (2.43 m) min
Co-linear horizontal run2 ft. (61 cm) max
Elbowsfour 45° or two 90°, not counting the 45° elbow at the stove
Cap discharge opening to roof surface18 in. (610 mm) min, horizontally
Floor opening10" X 10" inside, firestop at every floor
Exhaust restrictorfactory D (fully open); set to the matrix zone
Note: the manual prints the roof clearance as 18 in. (610 mm) on p. 10 (fig. 10 is labelled 18 min.), but pairs 610 mm with 24" on p. 6 and p. 7.

Terminate inside a shaded area of the vent termination matrix (fig. 9, p. 9). Support offsets with wall straps at three-foot intervals; prefer 45° elbows. Enclose venting exposed in living space above the first floor, keep 1" clearance on all sides, and retain attic insulation with a barrier. Steep roofs, nearby trees and wind can cause poor draft or down-draft; a taller vent may help.

Co-linear (masonry or Class A chimney)

Dual 3" flex liners; co-linear height 8 ft. min, 35 ft. max. Clean and inspect the flue first. Masonry needs a fireclay liner the full length; prefab chimneys must be UL 103 or ULC S-629 listed with a 6 inches (150 mm) minimum inside diameter. The air intake flex must extend 6 feet beyond the damper area. If the intake flex doesn't run the full length to the cap, a metal block-off plate above the unit must seal the flue from the room. A return loop in the intake helps prevent draft reversals. May require CPI mode.

Run level or rise 1/4 in. per foot toward the cap; never run downward. Use a vinyl siding standoff (Simpson Dura-Vent #950) on vinyl siding, and don't recess the cap. Break off the deflector flange if a snorkel isn't used. Exterior terminal clearances A–N (U.S. and Canada) are tabled on p. 13.

Snorkel terminations (p. 14)

14" snorkel: maximum 12" horizontal, no elbow. 36" snorkel: maximum horizontal run 6 ft. (182 cm); one 45° elbow allowed for a corner. Skirt extension plates need no adjustment; keep the exhaust restrictor at the factory setting (Position D - fully open).

conflicts.reason: Not one number printed two ways: p. 20's #158261 heads the identification table for the fiber log set packed in the firebox (with the six log part numbers), while p. 36 lists 157445 as the Replacement Log Set under Replacement Parts Not Illustrated, the same pattern the manual uses for other replacement kits (Glass Panel 220576 vs Replacement Glass & Gasket 155599 on p. 36). The guide shows both and says what each is.

review.notes: Page numbers are physical pages. The manual's table of contents and several internal cross-references are off by about one page from Gas Connection onward (e.g. Gas Pressure listed as 19 is on p. 18; the battery box 'fig. 45 on page 25' is really the control compartment, fig. 44 on p. 24). Decoded 29-code-point offset text: the running header on pp. 7, 9, 14, 17, 29 ('NPVQVR_oev_t dc PMM as fmf TLON' = '139495_Rev_W GF 300 DV IPI 7/21'); p. 7 'oequirements' = 'Requirements'; p. 9 'rp to four QR° or two VM°' = 'Up to four 45° or two 90°'; p. 17 'lineI ... clearJ' = 'line, ... clear-'; p. 29 MODE key text = 'CPI/IPI, Burner, Fan, and Accent Lamp.' plus figure labels 'Blue LCD Screen' and 'UP/DOWN Key'. Other scrambled fragments on pp. 7, 9, 14, 17 and 29 (figure labels) don't decode with that rule and were ignored. French-only: one sentence beside the high-altitude text on p. 18 was not translated; the specManifold drawer points to the page. The gas-smell blocks (pp. 1, 39) are in English. Figures not transcribed: minimum hearth protection (fig. 1, p. 6), clearance and mantel diagrams (figs. 2-4a, p. 7), vent termination matrix zones (fig. 9, p. 9), normal flame picture (fig. 43, p. 23), and the rear/top exit dimension drawings (p. 4). The exterior terminal clearance table A-N (p. 13) doesn't extract cleanly into its Canada/U.S. columns (and row E prints 12 in. with 46 cm), so it is only linked. IPI wording: p. 24 says the IPI pilot extinguishes after burner ignition, while p. 28 says once rectification occurs the unit remains lit; the guide only says the IPI pilot lights on a call for heat. Burner switch for the remote: p. 29 says ON; p. 24 says it stays ON for the remote but also lists T-STAT for wall thermostat or remote control; p. 39 says ON or T-STAT. The guide follows p. 29 and shows p. 24's descriptions. The remote, blower, accent lamp and flame control are accessories (pp. 26, 36), so the remote is described as optional; 'external regulator (for Propane only)' appears only in the suggested-tools list (p. 2). Minor: 8 ft. is given as 2.43 m (p. 10) and 2.44 m (p. 11); altitude ranges are 610 - 1371 m, 610-1370 m and 0-1372 m (p. 18); the high-altitude text cites ANSI Z21.88-2009 / CSA 2.33-2009 while the certification is the 2016 editions; p. 2 boilerplate calls the unit a fireplace insert. The ceiling clearance (61") and minimum alcove ceiling height from hearth (44 1/4") are measured from reference points shown only in the diagrams. Rear log part number 226892 (p. 20) breaks the 22489x pattern of the other five logs; possibly a typo. Catalog: heating area, overall dimensions and weight are not stated in the manual text, so they could not be checked; BTU inputs and P.4.1 efficiencies match. The catalog feature line says the backup is AA (see the battery conflict); the parts list (p. 33) also lists an Ivory enamel finish not in the catalog's finish list.
